misconceptions.title: which works for shell built-ins
misconceptions.misconception: which shows paths for all commands including built-ins
misconceptions.reality: which only shows paths for external executables, not shell built-ins (cd, history, etc.). Built-ins don't have paths. Use type command to check if something is a built-in.
misconceptions.tip: which only shows external commands. For built-ins (cd, history), use type command instead: type cd shows it's a built-in.

misconceptions.title: which shows aliases
misconceptions.misconception: which shows where aliases point to
misconceptions.reality: which doesn't expand aliases by default. Use type or alias command to see aliases. which shows the underlying executable, not alias definitions.
misconceptions.tip: Use type or alias to see aliases. which shows actual executable paths.

common_pitfalls.description: Expecting which to show paths for cd, history, etc.
common_pitfalls.solution: Built-ins don't have paths - they're part of the shell. Use type command to check if something is a built-in, external command, or alias.

common_pitfalls.description: Expecting which to show where aliases point
common_pitfalls.solution: Use type or alias commands to see aliases. which only shows actual executable paths in PATH.

common_pitfalls.issue: Command exists but which doesn't find it
common_pitfalls.description: Command works but which shows nothing
common_pitfalls.solution: Command might be a built-in or alias, or not in PATH. Use type to check. If it's an external command, verify PATH includes its directory.

best_practices: Use which to find executable paths quickly
Use which -a to see all versions in PATH
Use type for built-ins and aliases (more comprehensive)
Use which in scripts to check if command exists: if which command > /dev/null
Remember: which only shows external commands, not built-ins or aliases
Use which to debug 'command not found' errors
performance_tips: which is very fast - searches PATH directories only
PATH is usually short (5-10 directories) so search is instant
Use which -a only when needed (slightly slower than default)
